title: Electron Small Examples
description: Use these small Electron examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Know the two main sides
examples.description: Electron's main process manages desktop windows.
examples.code:
Main process: creates and manages windows.
Renderer process: displays HTML, CSS and page JavaScript.
Preload script: exposes a small approved bridge between them.
examples.output: The three roles help you decide where each kind of code belongs.

examples.title: Create a local window
examples.description: BrowserWindow creates a desktop window. Wait for app readiness before creating it, then load a local page.
examples.output: A local index.html file opens in an 800 by 600 window.

examples.title: Build the renderer page
examples.description: The renderer can use normal HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript.
examples.code: Reading club
examples.output: Save as index.html and create renderer.js for the button behaviour. Electron displays it as a normal local page.

examples.title: Set a restrictive page policy
examples.description: A Content Security Policy limits where a page can load and run content.
examples.code:
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:">
<!-- Put this in index.html head; use local external JS and CSS files. -->
examples.output: The page accepts the allowed local resources and blocks inline scripts under this policy.

examples.title: Configure a preload file
examples.description: A preload script runs before the page and can expose a small API.
examples.output: The named local preload file is loaded for that window before page scripts.

examples.title: Expose one harmless value
examples.description: contextBridge can expose a chosen value to the renderer without sharing full Node tools.
examples.output: The renderer can read the club name through window.club.

examples.title: Ask the main process a narrow question
examples.description: IPC lets the renderer ask the main process for an approved result.
examples.output: With the shown handler registered in main, the renderer can await window.club.getVersion().

examples.title: Handle a bridge failure
examples.description: A request through the bridge can reject.
examples.output: A successful request shows the version. A failed request shows the fallback text.

examples.title: Prevent unexpected navigation
examples.description: A local app window should not become an unrestricted browser for unknown content.
examples.output: The app denies renderer-driven page navigation and new-window requests for this simple local design.

examples.title: Keep a window reference
examples.description: The main process can keep a reference to its window and clear it when the window is closed.
examples.output: The variable points to the open window and becomes null after that window closes.

examples.title: Respect desktop lifecycle rules
examples.description: Desktop platforms have different conventions after all windows close.
examples.output: The app follows common close-and-reopen behaviour for the platform.

examples.title: Check the packaged app
examples.description: A packaged desktop app can behave differently from the development folder.
examples.code:
Use a maintained Electron packaging tool such as Electron Forge.
Build for a supported target platform.
Open the packaged app.
Check local images and scripts.
Test bridge success and failure.
Confirm no renderer Node access or unexpected new windows.
examples.output: The check finds missing bundled files and unsafe assumptions before sharing the app.
